title: Security requirements queue classifier and business-impact annotator
creator: Lena Park
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and channel partners submit a high volume of security/compliance asks (vendor questionnaires, SOC2/ISO evidence requests, DPAs, HIPAA questions). Triage is currently manual: routing to the right responder (security, legal, solutions), estimating business impact, and setting SLAs consumes time and causes SLA slippage for high-priority customers.

Goal: Build an automated queue classifier that routes incoming security/compliance requests into the correct intake lane (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaire, other) and produces a structured business-impact annotation (impact: low/medium/high; recommended SLA; likely responder group; evidence checklist). The feature should reduce manual triage time, prioritize real customer-impact requests, and create consistent routing for Dedicated/Private deals.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In-scope: classifier prototype for new inbound requests via support form and email; annotation pipeline that attaches suggested SLA and responder; lightweight attachment scanning for keywords (no content extraction beyond metadata) subject to security review; monitoring dashboard for model performance.
- Out-of-scope: full automatic answer generation to questionnaires, auto-responding to customers, or backend automated evidence collection in this phase.

Data sources and privacy: training will use historical triage labels (approx 6k tickets from 2023-2025), security taxonomy maintained by Security ops, and attachment metadata. All training data will be PII-sanitized. Raw customer attachments will not be persisted beyond 30 days for model training without explicit legal/security approval.

Approach: hybrid rule + ML classifier. Rules cover explicit keywords and known enterprise accounts; ML model (lightweight text classifier, e.g., fine-tuned transformer distil model or XGBoost on embeddings) handles ambiguous language and scores confidence. Confidence thresholds: >=0.85 auto-route; 0.6-0.85 route with "needs-review" flag; <0.6 escalate to human triage. Business-impact annotator combines model score, account tier, recent churn/risk signals, and request content to output impact label and recommended SLA.

Acceptance criteria (must be met for rollout):
- Top-1 routing precision >= 0.85 on validation set across SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA/vendor questionnaire classes.
- End-to-end median triage time reduced by >=40% for P1/P0 customer asks during a 2-week pilot.
- Security sign-off recorded on data handling and attachment scanning (security_review_required=true).
- Monitoring dashboard in Console showing per-class precision/recall, confidence distribution, and a human-feedback queue.

Metrics to track: routing precision/recall by class, avg manual touches per request, SLA miss rate by customer tier, false-positive escalation rate, and time-to-first-assign.

acceptance_criteria: Top-1 routing precision >= 0.85 on holdout validation across target classes
Pilot reduces median manual triage time by >= 40% for P0/P1 requests
Security team signs off on attachment handling and retention policy
Dashboard exposes per-class precision, confidence buckets, and manual-review queue
plan: Week 0-2: data collection, label harmonization with Security Ops and Support; finalize taxonomy
Week 3-4: build rule set and baseline classifier; implement PII sanitization and retention rules
Week 5: internal canary on 5% of traffic with human-in-loop review and feedback capture
Week 6: iterate on thresholds, integrate suggested SLA annotations, add dashboard widgets
Week 7-8: 2-week pilot with sales/accounting prioritized customers; collect metrics and manual feedback
Week 9: roll to 50% with rollout playbook and runbook for failures; security sign-off required before 100%
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Classifier misroutes high-impact asks. Mitigation: conservative confidence thresholds and human-in-loop for >=medium impact candidates; fallback route to Security Ops for appeals.

Risk: Attachment scanning exposes sensitive data. Mitigation: only use metadata/filename/size and hashed embeddings for training until KMS-approved pipeline exists; enforce 30-day retention and audit logs.
Risk: Model decay over time. Mitigation: weekly sampling of routed items for manual review and monthly retrain schedule; alerting on sudden shifts in confidence distribution.
Risk: Edge-case regulatory requests (local law). Mitigation: include 'jurisdiction' tag and escalate low-confidence jurisdiction requests to legal triage.
Risk: Stakeholder buy-in. Mitigation: involve Security and Support SMEs in label harmonization and early demos; include rollback plan and manual override in Console
